Porsche AG: luxury sports cars with China collapse, EV strategy reversal and tariffs hitting margins.

Renault: French carmaker revived by Dacia value brand and cost cuts; CEO change, European volume market.
Stellantis: 14 auto brands with heavy US exposure; inventory crisis, share loss and CEO change; union labour.
Volkswagen: world's #2 carmaker losing share in China, high labour costs, union-protected plants and software (CARIAD) struggles.

Valeo: French auto parts supplier; low margins, concentrated OEM customers.
AUTO1 Group: online used-car platform (Autohero) and dealer wholesale.

D'Ieteren: holding of Belron (Carglass), VW distribution in Belgium and TVH parts.

Zalando: largest European online fashion platform with ABOUT YOU acquisition; low margins, Shein competition.

Now focused on DCC Energy (LPG, fuel distribution, energy services) after exiting healthcare/tech; local density helps but end-market faces long-run energy-transition decline.

Games Workshop: owner of Warhammer IP with vertically integrated miniatures and Amazon licensing deal.

Heineken Holding: Heineken family holdco owning 50.005% of Heineken NV; same brewing economics at a holding discount.

B&M European Value Retail: UK discount variety retailer; weak like-for-likes and CEO change.
Marks & Spencer: UK food and clothing retailer whose turnaround lifted food share; brand trust is the main asset; cyber-attack disruption.

Diageo: world #1 spirits company (Johnnie Walker, Guinness, Don Julio); global spirits downturn, US tequila destocking and leadership changes.
Pernod Ricard: #2 global spirits group (Jameson, Absolut, Martell); China cognac tariffs and US downturn.

Beiersdorf: Nivea and premium La Prairie skincare plus tesa adhesives; La Prairie weakness offset by derma brands.
Galderma: pure-play dermatology across aesthetics, consumer skincare and prescription; aesthetics are discretionary but growing.

Greek refiner with efficient complex refinery; earnings swing with crack spreads.

Global independent tank-storage leader at strategic ports; contracted revenue; shifting from oil to gas, chemicals and new-energy storage.

Europe's largest asset manager with captive distribution through Crédit Agricole; passive fee pressure.

One of three Dutch banking oligopolists; state still a large shareholder; rate-sensitive NII.
Crédit Agricole SA: listed arm of France's mutualist group with Amundi and Predica insurance; distribution via regional banks gives stable fee income.

Banco BPM: Italy's third-largest bank, northern SME/retail focus; Crédit Agricole a key shareholder; rate-sensitive NII and consolidation politics.
Barclays: UK retail bank plus volatile global investment bank and US cards; restructuring to raise returns, still below cost of capital historically.
BBVA: digital leader with dominant Mexican franchise; EM currency risk; failed Sabadell bid.

DNB: Norway's dominant bank (~25-30% share) with leading asset management and Carnegie acquisition; high, stable ROE.

Jyske Bank: Danish universal bank with mortgage arm; steady but low-growth domestic franchise.
Ringkjøbing Landbobank: highly efficient Danish niche lender (cost/income ~25%) with strong credit record; small scale.
SpareBank 1 Sør-Norge: large merged Norwegian savings bank; strong regional deposit share; rate-sensitive.
Sparebanken Norge: merged Norwegian savings bank (Sparebanken Vest and Sør) with strong West/South Norway share; rate-sensitive margins.
Unicaja Banco: Andalusia-focused Spanish retail bank with large deposit base; low growth and limited pricing power.
Valiant: Swiss domestic retail bank expanding into new cantons; small, rate-sensitive, little differentiation.
Hannover Re: world's third-largest reinsurer with the lowest cost ratio in the industry; disciplined underwriting through the cycle.
Munich Re: world's largest reinsurer plus ERGO primary insurance; scale, data and capital strength allow disciplined pricing through the cycle.
SCOR: French reinsurer; life reserve charges and nat-cat volatility; weaker capital-generation record than peers.
Swiss Re: global #2 reinsurer; past reserve charges in US casualty; improving discipline.

moat: Single global platform (unified commerce) + technological lead
note: Adyen: Global leader in unified enterprise payment processing; single-codebase architecture delivers industry-leading authorization rates, low churn, and unmatched operational leverage, compounding at 25%+ ROIC.
Allfunds: largest B2B fund distribution platform; network effects between fund houses and distributors; fee pressure.
Edenred: multi-sided meal-voucher/employee-benefits network (merchants, employers, users); regulatory caps on fees in France/Italy hurt pricing.
Nexi: Italian/Nordic merchant acquirer and card processor; losing share and pricing to newer platforms; low growth.
Wise: cross-border payments infrastructure that cuts prices as scale grows (intentional price-giveback); growing Wise Platform for banks; take-rate deliberately falling.
Abivax: clinical-stage biotech whose value rests on obefazimod in ulcerative colitis; no commercial revenue yet, binary regulatory and commercial risk.
argenx: Vyvgart is the leading FcRn blocker for myasthenia gravis and CIDP with expanding indications; competition from J&J/UCB FcRn drugs.
Genmab: royalties on J&J's Darzalex plus own oncology products; Darzalex royalty expiry and Merus acquisition integration are key risks.
Grifols: #2-3 plasma-derived therapies with large collection network; governance and leverage concerns after short-seller report.
Sobi: Swedish rare-disease specialist (haemophilia, immunology) growing via in-licensing and acquisitions; product concentration risk.
Zealand Pharma: Danish peptide biotech with Roche-partnered obesity drug.
Galenica: Switzerland's largest pharmacy chain (Amavita, Sun Store) and wholesaler; regulated drug prices limit pricing power.
Alcon: global #1 in ophthalmic surgical equipment and consumables plus contact lenses; surgeons trained on its platforms, ageing-population cataract demand.
bioMérieux: world leader in microbiology and syndromic (BioFire) diagnostics with reagent pull-through on installed instruments.
Demant: one of five hearing-aid makers with retail clinics; replacement cycles ~4-5 years; OTC and Apple AirPods hearing features as substitutes.
EssilorLuxottica: dominant in lenses and frames with owned retail and smart glasses (Meta Ray-Ban); vision correction is non-discretionary.
Getinge: infection control, ICU ventilation and cardiac assist; quality-remediation history in the US.
Philips: health-tech with imaging and monitoring installed base; Respironics recall damage and China weakness.
Sectra: Swedish medical imaging IT and cybersecurity with long contracts and high retention.
Siemens Healthineers: imaging, diagnostics and Varian radiotherapy with large service installed base; China weakness and diagnostics restructuring.
Smith & Nephew: orthopaedics, sports medicine and advanced wound care; years of execution problems and share loss in knees/hips.
Sonova: hearing aids (Phonak), cochlear implants and audiological care clinics; hearing-aid oligopoly with OTC threats.
Fresenius Medical Care: global #1 dialysis provider; labour costs, reimbursement pressure and GLP-1 impact on kidney disease volumes.
Fresenius: Kabi (IV generics, nutrition, biosimilars) and Helios hospitals in Germany/Spain; regulated reimbursement and labour costs.
Coloplast: #1 in ostomy and intermittent catheters with daily-use consumables and strong user loyalty; wound-care and voice-care weaker.
ConvaTec: ostomy, continence, advanced wound care and infusion sets; recurring consumables, but #2-3 positions and US reimbursement (LCD) risk.
Straumann: global #1 premium dental implants and clear aligners; strong brand among clinicians.
Sartorius Stedim Biotech: single-use bioprocessing (bags, filters, bioreactors) validated into customers' drug filings, creating switching costs.
Eurofins: largest testing lab network (food, environment, pharma, clinical); fragmented customers, but heavy capex and governance criticism.
Lonza: leading biologics CDMO; customer molecules validated at its sites create high switching costs; capacity investment heavy.
QIAGEN: sample-preparation consumables and QIAstat syndromic testing; recurring reagent revenue and life-science exposure.
Siegfried: Swiss small-molecule CDMO with drug-product capabilities; customer validation creates moderate stickiness.
Sartorius: bioprocess consumables plus lab products; single-use demand recovered after destocking bust.
Tecan: lab automation and OEM liquid-handling components; biopharma and diagnostics capex weakness.
ALK-Abelló: world leader in allergy immunotherapy tablets with registered products that are costly to replicate; niche market, steady double-digit growth.
AstraZeneca: broad oncology, CVRM and rare-disease portfolio with one of the most productive pipelines; US drug-pricing and China risks.
Bayer: pharma patent cliffs (Xarelto), glyphosate litigation and high debt; crop science cyclical; restructuring under DSO model.
GSK: vaccines (Shingrix) and ViiV HIV franchise with specialty medicines; dolutegravir patent cliff late decade.
Hikma: US generic injectables and MENA branded pharma; price deflation in generics.
Ipsen: French specialty pharma facing Somatuline generic erosion, relying on rare-disease launches.
Merck KGaA: life science (MilliporeSigma), healthcare and electronics; diversified but recently soft across segments.
Novartis: pure-play innovative medicines (Entresto, Kisqali, Pluvicto); strong execution after Sandoz spin.

Novo Nordisk: Global metabolic leader sharing an entrenched worldwide GLP-1 duopoly with Eli Lilly; multi-billion dollar manufacturing fill-finish scale, vast patent portfolio, and non-discretionary patient demand provide volume predictability and pricing resilience.
Orion: Finnish pharma with Nubeqa (prostate cancer) royalties via Bayer, Nordic generics and animal health; concentrated profit driver.
Recordati: Italian specialty and rare-disease pharma with steady growth and high margins; acquisitive.
Roche: world #1 in in-vitro diagnostics (huge reagent-driven installed base) plus oncology/immunology pharma; diversified pipeline offsets biosimilar erosion of legacy antibodies.
Sanofi: Dupixent (immunology blockbuster) plus vaccines and rare diseases; strong growth but high concentration in one drug before its 2031 patent expiry.
Sandoz: global generics and biosimilars leader with cost-of-goods scale; structurally deflationary pricing in generics; biosimilar wave is the growth driver.
UCB: Belgian biopharma propelled by Bimzelx (psoriasis/HS) and epilepsy franchise; patent concentration risk.
Airbus: commercial aircraft duopoly with Boeing and decade-long backlog; supply chain (engines) bottlenecks limit deliveries.
Dassault Aviation: Rafale export success and Falcon jets; concentrated programmes, French state customer.
BAE Systems: UK's defence champion with US electronics and submarines; long-term government programmes with rearmament tailwind.
Babcock International: UK naval and nuclear support contractor (submarines, dockyards); programme-concentrated but long-dated government work.
CSG: Czech defence group (ammunition, vehicles) listed 2026; rearmament boom; concentrated ownership.
Hensoldt: German defence sensors and radar maker with rearmament-driven backlog.
Thales: defence electronics, avionics, cybersecurity and digital identity; long government programmes and rearmament tailwinds.
Indra: Spanish defence electronics, air-traffic management and IT (Minsait); benefits from European rearmament; state-influenced.
Kongsberg: Norwegian defence (NASAMS air defence, NSM missiles) and maritime technology; strong order backlog and niche technology leadership.
Leonardo: Italian defence, helicopters and electronics with Iveco Defence acquisition; state-controlled; rearmament tailwinds.
Melrose: pure-play GKN Aerospace engine structures and components with risk-and-revenue-sharing partnerships giving long aftermarket tails.
MTU Aero Engines: German partner in PW1100G GTF and V2500 engines with large MRO business; GTF powder-metal issue a temporary drag.
QinetiQ: UK/US defence testing, evaluation and research services; US business underperforming.
RENK: German maker of military vehicle transmissions and industrial gearboxes; rearmament-driven backlog.
Rheinmetall: German ammunition, armoured vehicles and air defence champion booming on European rearmament; capacity-constrained, government demand cyclical over decades.
Rolls-Royce: widebody aero-engine duopolist (with GE) earning lifetime service revenue on Trent fleet; turnaround lifted margins; also defence and power systems.
Saab: Swedish defence group (Gripen fighters, GlobalEye, Carl-Gustaf, sensors) benefiting from Nordic rearmament and NATO enlargement.
Safran: 50% of CFM (LEAP/CFM56) narrowbody engines with decades of aftermarket revenue, plus landing gear and cabin; supply-chain constraints but superb pricing.
DHL Group: global express leader plus freight forwarding and German post; cyclical trade volumes, unionised postal labour.
DSV: global #1 freight forwarder after DB Schenker deal; integration track record strong but freight volumes cyclical.
Kuehne+Nagel: global #1 sea freight forwarder and top-3 air; asset-light but cyclical volumes and rates.
Aéroports de Paris: operator of CDG and Orly under regulated concessions plus international stakes (GMR); regulatory friction with the French state.
Aena: owns/operates 46 Spanish airports plus Luton and Brazil; regulated tariffs, rising commercial revenues; strong tourism demand.
Flughafen Zürich: Zurich airport monopoly with regulated aviation and growing commercial income.
ASSA ABLOY: global #1 in locks and access solutions with ~2/3 aftermarket; serial acquirer with pricing power.
Belimo: global #1 in HVAC damper actuators and control valves; data-centre cooling and building-efficiency regulation drive growth.
Geberit: European leader in concealed cisterns and piping; installer loyalty and spec-in make it a price leader in a renovation-driven market.
Kingspan: global leader in insulated panels and building envelopes; energy-efficiency regulation tailwinds but construction-cycle exposure.
NIBE: heat pumps and climate solutions; European heat-pump demand collapsed after subsidy changes, now recovering.
Rockwool: global stone-wool insulation leader benefiting from energy-efficiency regulation.
Saint-Gobain: building materials and light construction (plaster, glass, insulation) with distribution; renovation-driven, cyclical new build.
ACS: global contractor via Hochtief and Turner with data-centre and PPP concessions; thin construction margins, low switching costs.
Arcadis: Dutch design/engineering consultancy for water, mobility and places; talent-dependent; low barriers.
BAM: Dutch construction group with thin margins and fixed-price risk.
Balfour Beatty: UK/US construction and infrastructure investments; thin contracting margins but strong cash position.
Vinci: French motorway concessions, airports (Gatwick, Lisbon) and global contracting/energy services; inflation-linked tolls but French concessions end in the 2030s.
Bouygues: French conglomerate spanning Colas roadbuilding, Bouygues Construction, Equans energy services, Bouygues Telecom and TF1; diversified but low-margin.
Eiffage: French contractor owning APRR motorway concessions; tolls are inflation-linked but concession maturities loom.
Bilfinger: industrial maintenance and engineering services for process industries; low barriers but sticky site relationships.
GEK Terna: Greek construction and concessions group (Attiki Odos motorway, Egnatia, Kastelli airport); state-linked projects.
Hochtief: ACS-controlled holding of Turner (booming US data-centre construction) and Australia's CIMIC; contracting margins are thin.
Sacyr: Spanish group shifting to infrastructure concessions (motorways, hospitals in Chile, Colombia, Spain) from construction; high leverage.
Skanska: Swedish/US construction and property development; contracting has thin margins, development cyclical.
SPIE: European multi-technical services for electrical, mechanical and digital infrastructure; energy-transition and data-centre demand, bolt-on acquisitions.
Technip Energies: top-2 LNG process engineering contractor; lumpy project awards from concentrated customers.
Alstom: #2 global rolling stock maker after Bombardier deal; low-margin legacy contracts and cash burn; signalling/services better.
Daimler Truck: global truck leader (Mercedes-Benz Trucks, Freightliner) with strong North American share; cyclical orders and emission-rule transitions.
Epiroc: mining and infrastructure equipment with ~2/3 aftermarket and automation leadership; commodity-capex cyclical.
FLSmidth: mining technology and services after selling cement business; large aftermarket share.
Hiab: load-handling equipment (HIAB cranes, MOFFETT forklifts) spun out of Cargotec; construction and trucking-cycle exposure.
Iveco Group: trucks and buses being acquired by Tata Motors; cyclical, low margins.
Metso: minerals processing and aggregates equipment with a large aftermarket share in wear parts and services; mining-capex sensitive.
Volvo Group: global truck leader (Volvo, Mack, Renault Trucks) with strong service business; cyclical truck orders and electrification capex.
Weir Group: mining wear parts and pumps with ~70% aftermarket; installed base at mine sites provides recurring revenue.
Amadeus: global distribution system network linking airlines and travel agents plus airline/hotel IT; high switching costs, but NDC direct-distribution threat.
Teleperformance: world's largest call-centre outsourcer; generative-AI customer service threatens its labour-based model directly.
Ayvens (ALD+LeasePlan): largest multi-brand car lessor; used-car residual-value risk; Société Générale-controlled.
Elis: European textile rental and hygiene services with route density.
ISS: global facility services provider with low margins, labour intensity and contract-loss risk.
Mitie: UK facilities management and security outsourcing; low margins, contract-renewal driven.
Serco: UK/international government-services outsourcer (immigration, defence, health); low margins and political contract risk.

Lagercrantz: Swedish serial acquirer of niche B2B tech companies with proprietary products; decentralised model, high returns.
Legrand: electrical wiring devices and data-centre infrastructure; spec-in by electricians and many niche leaderships drive steady pricing.

Schneider Electric: global leader in low/medium-voltage electrical distribution and energy management with software (AVEVA); data-centre and electrification demand drive pricing power.

moat: Pest control route density + efficient scale
note: Rentokil Initial: Global #1 commercial pest control operator; unmatched local route density creates superior technician utilization and operating margin moats, supported by non-discretionary regulatory compliance contracts and resilient 15%+ ROIC.

Vestas: global #1 wind turbine maker with large service backlog; onshore turbines price-competitive vs Chinese OEMs; offshore losses.

moat: Toll-road concessions (407 ETR, US managed lanes)
note: Ferrovial: 407 ETR toll road and US managed lanes with dynamic pricing.

Randstad: world's largest staffing company; cyclical temp demand, AI pressure on clerical roles.
Lifco: Swedish acquirer of niche businesses in dental distribution, demolition robots (Brokk) and systems solutions; decentralised, high-return.
Metlen: Greek industrial group in aluminium, energy and infrastructure; moved listing to London.
Siemens: industrial automation and digital-industries software (Xcelerator), smart infrastructure and Mobility; deep installed base in factory automation, though China and automation destocking hurt.
Smiths Group: detection, Flex-Tek and John Crane mechanical seals being separated; niche positions but conglomerate history.
Aalberts: Dutch maker of installation technology (pipe fittings), industrial niches and surface treatments; cyclical building and semicap exposure.
Accelleron: global #1 in large turbochargers for ships and power plants with ~80% service revenue from a huge installed base; decarbonisation risk long-term.
Alfa Laval: global #1 in heat exchangers, separators and marine fluid handling with ~30% service; energy transition and data-centre cooling demand.

moat: Hydro, pulp & paper and metals equipment
note: Andritz: Austrian plant equipment for hydropower, pulp/paper and metals; project-driven, growing service share.
Atlas Copco: global leader in compressors, vacuum and industrial tools with high service share; decentralised, strong pricing power.
GEA Group: process equipment for dairy, food, beverage and pharma with growing service share; project-driven demand.
Georg Fischer: now a pure piping-systems company after selling its machining and casting units; integrating Finland's Uponor; building and utility-water cycles.
Hill & Smith: road safety barriers, galvanizing and engineered solutions mostly in the US.
IMI: flow-control niches (precision engineering, hydronics, process valves) with aftermarket; repositioned to higher-margin markets.
Interpump: Italian world leader in high-pressure plunger pumps and hydraulics; acquisitive niche leader.
Knorr-Bremse: global #1 braking systems for rail and trucks with large aftermarket; truck-cycle exposure.
Konecranes: industrial cranes and port equipment with a large service business; port-equipment orders lumpy and cyclical.
KION: forklift trucks (Linde, STILL) and Dematic warehouse automation; cyclical capex and Chinese forklift competition.
KONE: global elevator/escalator maker earning recurring maintenance and modernisation revenue on a huge installed base; China new-build slump.
Rational: global leader in professional combi-steamers for commercial kitchens with high margins; restaurant-capex cyclical.
Rotork: valve actuators with installed base and aftermarket; process industries.
Rosebank Industries: UK vehicle founded by ex-Melrose managers to buy, improve and sell industrial businesses; first deal ECI.
Sandvik: global #1 in cutting tools (Sandvik Coromant) plus mining equipment and services; high aftermarket share, industrial-cycle sensitive.
Schindler: #2 global elevator maker with service-driven recurring revenue; China new-build weakness.
SFS Group: Swiss precision fasteners and components; industrial cycles.
SKF: global #1 bearings maker separating its automotive business; industrial-cycle exposure, Asian competition.
Spirax Group: steam systems and peristaltic pumps sold via direct sales engineers; recurring maintenance demand.
Sulzer: pumps, flow equipment and chemtech services; service-heavy but cyclical process industries.
Tomra: reverse-vending machines and sorting technology driven by deposit-return regulation.
Trelleborg: engineered polymer solutions for aerospace, healthcare and industry; serial niche acquirer.
Valmet: pulp, board/tissue and energy technology plus automation with ~50% services; pulp/paper capex cyclical.
Wärtsilä: marine engines and power plants with large service base; decarbonisation drives retrofits.
Crude tanker owner; day rates swing violently with freight cycles and sanctions; no pricing power, pure spot-market exposure.
A.P. Moller-Maersk: container shipping and integrated logistics; freight rates swing violently with capacity and geopolitics (Red Sea).
easyJet: low-cost airline with primary-airport slots and growing holidays business; cost base above Ryanair.
IAG: owner of British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus, Vueling with Heathrow/Madrid slots.
Lufthansa: German hub airline group with union strikes and cost issues.

moat: Lowest cost base in European aviation
note: Ryanair: Europe's lowest-cost airline with Boeing 737 fleet advantage and ancillary revenue; aircraft delivery delays and fuel costs.
Bureau Veritas: global testing, inspection and certification (marine, buildings, commodities); regulation-driven, fragmented customers.
Experian: global #1 consumer credit bureau with proprietary data, decisioning software and consumer services; lending-cycle sensitive.
Intertek: global testing, inspection and certification for consumer goods, energy and industry; fragmented customers and steady regulatory demand.
RELX: LexisNexis legal, Elsevier scientific, risk analytics and exhibitions; proprietary datasets embedded in professional workflows with AI tools layered on top.
SGS: world's #1 testing, inspection and certification company; regulation-driven and fragmented customers, but low switching costs per job.
Sweco: Europe's largest engineering and architecture consultancy, Swedish-based; utilisation-driven and talent-dependent with few structural barriers.
Wolters Kluwer: expert software and information (UpToDate, CCH tax, legal) embedded in professional workflows; 80%+ recurring revenue.
Loomis: cash-handling and ATM logistics with route density; secular decline of cash use in Nordics/US.
Securitas: global security services provider shifting from manned guarding toward technology-enabled solutions; labour-intensive, low-margin and union-exposed.
Verisure: Europe's leading monitored home-alarm provider with ~5m subscribers; recurring revenue and low churn.
Addtech: Swedish serial acquirer of niche technical trading and manufacturing firms; decentralised, high return on working capital.
Beijer Ref: largest independent refrigeration/HVAC wholesaler in Europe/APAC; refrigerant regulation drives replacement.
Brenntag: world's largest chemicals distributor; weak industrial volumes, restructuring and low switching costs.
Bunzl: distributes consumables (packaging, cleaning, safety) to foodservice, retail and healthcare; recent margin issues.
DKSH: outsourced distribution in Asia for consumer, healthcare and specialty goods; thin margins.
Diploma: decentralised distributor of essential niche components (seals, controls, fasteners); high margins and consistent growth.
Howden Joinery: UK trade-only kitchen supplier with local depot density and builder credit relationships.

Indutrade: Swedish serial acquirer of ~200 niche industrial technology companies; decentralised model with high returns on capital.
RS Group: multichannel distributor of industrial and electronic components to engineers; weak industrial volumes and digital competition.
Rexel: electrical supplies distributor in Europe/North America; electrification tailwind, thin distribution margins.
tk accelis: thyssenkrupp's materials distribution and supply-chain services spin-off (listed 28 Oct 2026); market leader in Europe but ~2-3% EBITDA margins.
Dassault Systèmes: 3D design/PLM standard in aerospace and auto plus Medidata life sciences; growth slowed, life-science weakness.
Nemetschek: AEC design software (Allplan, Graphisoft, Bluebeam, Vectorworks) moving to subscription; deep workflow integration.
Octave: software spun off from Hexagon in 2026 (asset lifecycle intelligence, geospatial); new standalone listing, limited track record.

Sage: SMB accounting and payroll software in UK/US/Europe; accountant networks and compliance lock in customers.
Temenos: core-banking software with long switching cycles; short-seller report, CEO turnover and slow cloud transition.
Ericsson: #2 in 5G RAN with Nokia/Huawei; telcos' capex cycle in decline; customers concentrated and price-driven.
Nokia: mobile networks, network infrastructure (Infinera) and patent licensing; telco capex decline offset by data-centre optics.
Hexagon: precision metrology, geospatial and reality-capture technology; spun off Octave software; embedded in manufacturing quality workflows.
Halma: decentralised group of ~50 niche safety, environmental and medical technology companies with regulatory-driven demand and consistent growth.
INFICON: vacuum gauges and leak detection for semiconductor and industrial markets; niche leader, semicap cyclical.
AT&S: high-end PCBs and IC substrates for AMD/Intel; heavy capex in Malaysia, concentrated customers and cyclical utilisation.

Computacenter: IT infrastructure reseller and services to large enterprises in UK/Germany/US; thin margins, hyperscaler deals lumpy.

note: Softcat: UK IT reseller with strong sales culture and customer growth; low switching costs.
Grupa Kęty: Polish aluminium extrusions and flexible packaging with high margins.

Croda: specialty ingredients for beauty, pharma (lipids) and crop care; destocking and pharma weakness.
dsm-firmenich: flavours, fragrances and nutrition ingredients after selling animal nutrition; co-development with customers but restructuring ongoing.
EMS-Chemie: Swiss maker of high-performance polyamides replacing metal in cars and industry; very high margins, auto-cycle exposure, Blocher family control.
Evonik: German specialty chemicals with commodity exposure; weak volumes and restructuring.
FUCHS: world's largest independent lubricants maker with specialty products and pricing power.
Givaudan: global #1 in flavours and fragrances; formulas co-developed with FMCG customers create very high switching costs and steady pricing.
Johnson Matthey: PGM-based autocatalysts and refining; hydrogen strategy scaled back; ICE decline long-term.
Novonesis: global #1 in industrial enzymes and microbes (Novozymes + Chr. Hansen); bio-solutions co-developed with customers, steady pricing.
Sika: global construction chemicals and adhesives leader serving repair, waterproofing and infrastructure; distribution scale and pricing power.
Symrise: flavours, fragrances, cosmetic ingredients and pet-food palatants; co-development with customers, growth slowing from high levels.
Syensqo: Belgian specialty polymers/materials spun from Solvay; aerospace composites and battery materials weakness.
Umicore: Belgian catalysts, recycling and battery materials; EV-battery cathode business written down heavily.
Acerinox: stainless steel producer whose US unit North American Stainless is the profit engine; commodity pricing and Chinese overcapacity.
ArcelorMittal: global steelmaker with mining assets; spreads are cyclical, European carbon costs and Chinese exports pressure prices.
SSAB: Swedish high-strength steel niche leader moving to fossil-free steel; cyclical prices.
thyssenkrupp: steel, marine systems (TKMS), materials services and automotive; restructuring, spin-offs and steel losses.
voestalpine: Austrian specialty steel and processing; auto and energy exposure.
British Land: London office campuses (Broadgate, Regent's Place) and retail parks; office demand uncertain.
Covivio: diversified European REIT with offices, residential and hotels.
Landsec: UK REIT with London offices, major shopping centres and residential pipeline; office demand uncertain.
Merlin Properties: Spain's largest REIT (Madrid/Barcelona offices, logistics) now pivoting capital into hyperscale data centres; development risk.

moat: Healthcare real estate (care homes) in Europe
note: Aedifica: Belgian REIT with ~600 care homes and healthcare properties across Europe; ageing demographics, inflation-linked triple-net leases; operator health risk.
Primary Health Properties: UK/Irish GP surgeries with NHS-backed rents; merged with Assura.
Tritax Big Box: UK logistics warehouses with long leases to Amazon and others; tenant concentration.
LondonMetric: UK triple-net REIT with logistics, convenience and entertainment assets; long leases.
Sagax: Nordic and European light-industrial and warehouse properties with high occupancy and low cost of capital.
SEGRO: UK and European urban warehouses plus data-centre land bank in Slough; high occupancy and rental growth.
WDP: Benelux/Romanian logistics REIT with in-house development and high occupancy.
Derwent London: central London office landlord for creative tenants; hybrid working and refurbishment capex pressure returns.
Gecina: prime central Paris offices with residential; low vacancy in core Paris.
Unite: largest UK student accommodation; international student visa policy risk.
Allreal: Swiss real-estate owner and developer focused on the Zurich region; low growth, rate-sensitive valuation.
Fastighets Balder: Swedish property company with residential, commercial and hotel assets; leveraged and rate-sensitive.
Castellum: largest Nordic listed commercial property company; office vacancies, refinancing costs and a rights issue after the rate shock.
LEG Immobilien: German affordable residential; rent regulation caps growth but low vacancy.
Mobimo: Swiss property developer and owner; low growth, rate-sensitive.
PSP Swiss Property: prime Swiss office/retail portfolio in Zurich/Geneva; conservative balance sheet.

moat: Swiss commercial real estate + asset management
note: Swiss Prime Site: largest Swiss listed real-estate company with prime offices plus a real-estate asset management arm.
TAG Immobilien: German secondary residential plus Polish rental build-out.
Vonovia: Germany's largest residential landlord (~540k flats) with near-full occupancy; rent regulation caps upside and leverage is high.

moat: Shopping centre scale in Continental Europe
note: Klépierre: Europe's #2 mall owner with dominant regional malls; e-commerce substitution limited by footfall recovery.
Shaftesbury Capital: Covent Garden and Carnaby estates in London's West End.
Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield: owner of flagship European and US malls; high leverage and exit from US remain the key issues.
Cellnex: Europe's largest independent tower operator with long inflation-linked contracts; concentrated MNO tenants and high leverage.
BKW: Bern-based utility with grids, hydro/nuclear generation and fast-growing engineering services.
EDP: Portuguese utility with Iberian networks and EDPR renewables stake; renewables returns pressured.
Endesa: Spanish integrated utility controlled by Enel; regulated networks plus nuclear/renewables generation.
Elia: TSO monopoly in Belgium and eastern Germany (50Hertz) with huge regulated capex for offshore grids.
Enel: Europe's largest private network operator plus a big renewables fleet across Italy, Spain and Latin America; regulatory and political exposure in several countries.
Iberdrola: regulated electricity networks in the US (Avangrid), UK (ScottishPower), Spain and Brazil plus large renewables fleet; best-in-class execution and network-led growth plan.
National Grid: monopoly electricity transmission in England/Wales and networks in New York/Massachusetts; very large regulated capex plan funded by a rights issue.
Public Power Corporation: Greece's dominant integrated utility, privatised and investing in renewables and grids.
Redeia: Spanish electricity transmission system operator with a regulated monopoly, plus Hispasat satellites and fibre; regulator sets returns.
SSE: UK electricity networks and leading offshore wind developer; regulated network growth plus merchant renewables exposure.
Terna: Italian electricity transmission monopoly with large regulated capex plan; stable returns.
Verbund: Austrian hydro-power generator with low-cost, low-carbon output; power price exposure.
Enagás: Spanish gas TSO with cut regulated returns and hydrogen network optionality.
Italgas: Italian gas distribution monopoly enlarged by 2i Rete Gas acquisition; regulated returns.
Rubis: LPG and fuel distribution in islands, Africa and Caribbean plus renewables; niche positions.
Snam: Italian gas transmission and storage monopoly with regulated returns plus hydrogen/CCS optionality and stakes in European pipelines.
Drax: UK biomass generation dependent on subsidies (CfD bridge from 2027) and sustainability scrutiny; pumped storage is a hidden gem.
Fortum: Finnish low-cost hydro and nuclear generator selling into the Nordic power market; earnings follow volatile power prices.
RWE: Germany's largest generator shifting to renewables and flexible gas plants; merchant power price exposure and heavy capex.
A2A: Milan/Brescia multi-utility with regulated networks, waste-to-energy and hydro generation; part merchant power exposure.

moat: British Gas customer base + gas storage/nuclear stakes
note: Centrica: British Gas retail supply, trading and nuclear/Rough storage; retail margins regulated by Ofgem price cap.
Engie: French utility with regulated gas/power networks, renewables, LNG and thermal generation; state-anchored, merchant power exposure.
E.ON: Europe's largest distribution-network operator with a growing regulated asset base from the energy transition; retail supply alongside.
Hera: Italian multi-utility in Emilia-Romagna with waste management, water and gas networks; steady regulated growth.
Naturgy: Spanish gas and power utility with regulated networks and merchant generation; ownership changes.
Veolia: global leader in water, waste and energy services with long municipal/industrial contracts; recurring, inflation-indexed revenue.
Acciona: Spanish infrastructure builder plus Acciona Energía renewables; power price weakness and leverage.
EDP Renováveis: global wind/solar developer; asset rotation model hit by rates and US policy.
Ørsted: offshore wind pioneer hit by US project cancellations, impairments and a rights issue; contracted but capital-intensive.
Pennon: South West Water and Bristol Water regulated monopoly; pollution and water-quality incidents.
Severn Trent: regulated water and wastewater monopoly in the English Midlands with best-in-class Ofwat performance record.
United Utilities: regulated water/wastewater monopoly in North West England; Ofwat price-review and environmental fine risks.
